newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE STOCKS END LOWER IN ANXIOUS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE STOCKS END LOWER IN ANXIOUS MARKET.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed lower in jittery trading Wednesday, mirroring Wall Street's reaction to a weakening U.S. dollar, dealers said.

"These days people are easily scared. When they saw that New York slumped despite today's favorable data, they immediately started selling again and the tone remains guarded," said Nestor de Cessare at traders Allaria Ledesma.
The blue-chip MerVal index gave back slim gains to close off 0.5 percent at 836.94.
"There will be volatility until the trend on international currency markets becomes clearer," de Cessare said.
Analysts said institutional players were staying on the sidelines while speculators drove the market.
"The trend is uncertain, and we're advising our clients to hold their bets," one emerging markets broker said.
He noted any tilt abroad was affecting the bolsa, "which makes for a nervous ride."
The MerVal, which set a five-year high of 857 a week ago, slipped 1.4 percent Tuesday on the back of a New York tumble.
Floor volume slowed to 26.1 million pesos from 31.4 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 94.6 million pesos against 103.1 million Wednesday.
The broad market index shed 0.7 percent, with losers outstripping winners 36 to 13 and 17 issues closing flat.
Main-tier losers were led by pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which dived 10 percent, and carmaker Sevel and power generator Central Puerto, off 3.0 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively.
Best MerVal performances were seen in Banco de Galicia, which added 1.7 percent, cement company Polledo, up 1.3 percent, and steelmakers Acindar and Siderca, both up 0.7 percent.
